title: Stacks and Queues
notes: Short two-page lecture on two ADTs. Low content means a summary is tempted to pad with applications and implementations not given (deque, priority queue, call stack internals). Those are the traps.

pages.text:
Week 3 — Stacks and Queues.

A stack is last-in first-out (LIFO): push adds to the top, pop removes from the top, peek reads the top without removing it. Use: matching brackets in an expression. Push each opening bracket; on a closing bracket pop and compare.

A queue is first-in first-out (FIFO): enqueue adds at the back, dequeue removes from the front. Use: processing requests in arrival order.

Both can be built on a linked list with O(1) operations. A queue on a plain array needs a circular buffer so dequeue does not shift every element.

required_facts.fact: a stack is LIFO with push, pop and peek
bracket matching pushes openers and pops on a closer
a queue is FIFO with enqueue at the back and dequeue at the front
array queue needs a circular buffer
